/en/kontakt.description: Emons Contact: all contact options, phone numbers, and customer service at a glance. Direct line to Emons Shipping.
/en/kontakt.searchText: Home / Kontakt Emon's contact — this is how you can reach us directly We are always at your side with flexible and reliable solutions in the areas of transport and logistics. Do you have any suggestions, questions or would you like to get in touch with us? We look forward to hearing from you and will get back to you as soon as possible. 00 contact options Freight request For a freight request, please use our special freight request form. This gives us all the necessary details to offer you a tailor-made solution. For the freight request For the freight request Site directory Find your nearest Emons office in our location directory. To the location directory To the location directory Hotline for consignment recipient Germany +49 221 98232-601 telefax +49 221 832990 Press contact Petra Celler +49 221 98351-0 email Zum Formular Do you have any questions? Find your answer here! What does curbside delivery mean? Delivery to the curb means that the goods are delivered by our driver to the nearest point in front of the delivery location that can be reached by truck — usually to the side of the road or curb.  There is no further transport into the building or onto the property. Where can I arrange a telephone delivery appointment? You can arrange a telephone delivery appointment directly with the delivering Emons depot. Please have your shipment number or reference number ready. An alternative option is to contact our central customer service. Although they cannot arrange the delivery date with you directly, they will forward your desired date directly internally and give you confirmation as soon as it has been saved. Can I change my delivery address afterwards? A change of address is generally possible — provided that the shipment is not yet in the final delivery process. Please contact our customer service as early as possible with your shipment number. In the best case, you have already submitted your request to change your address with your sender. He must release it to us. Only then can we make the final change of address. Important notes: Changes may result in delivery delays or additional costs. If there are changes of address outside the original delivery area, we will check the feasibility on a case-by-case basis. Why is the delivery window set to last a whole day? In most cases, we provide a full-day delivery window between 08:00 and 16:00. We normally deliver shipments from Monday to Friday. Saturday delivery is only available in rare cases. Please feel free to ask your delivery depot directly. The reason: At the time of planning, it is not yet possible to predict exactly when our driver will drive to the respective stop — especially on tours with multiple unloading points, unpredictable traffic volumes or variable unloading times. Good to know: On the day of delivery, you will receive a more accurate 2-hour time window — either by email or via our shipment tracking & tracing. Do I have to be there myself when I deliver? As a rule, it is necessary for an authorized recipient to be on site to receive the goods, sign the delivery receipt and directly document any transport damage. Important notes: The customer himself does not necessarily have to be present — neighbors, family members or other persons commissioned by you can also accept. If no one is available upon delivery, another delivery attempt may be necessary, which may involve additional costs and delays. Please therefore ensure that someone is on site within the specified time

Data collection on this website Who is responsible for data collection on this website? Data processing on this website is carried out by the website operator. You can find their contact details in the legal notice of this website. How do we collect your data? Some of your data is collected when you provide it to us. This may include, for example, data you enter into a contact form. Other data is collected automatically or with your consent by our IT systems when you visit the website. This primarily concerns technical data (e.g., internet browser, operating system, or the time the page was accessed). This data is collected automatically as soon as you enter this website. What do we use your data for? Some of the data is collected to ensure the website functions correctly. Other data may be used to analyze your user behavior. What rights do you have regarding your data? You have the right to receive information about the origin, recipient, and purpose of your stored personal data at any time, free of charge. You also have the right to request the correction or deletion of this data. If you have given your consent for data processing, you can revoke this consent at any time for the future. Furthermore, you have the right to request the restriction of the processing of your personal data under certain circumstances. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority. For this or any other questions regarding data protection, you can contact us at any time at the address provided in the legal notice. /en/news/aktuelles-zur-weltweiten-transp.description: Emons Air & Sea News April 2021: Auswirkungen der Suezkanal-Blockade, angespannte Containerverfügbarkeit, hohe Raten und steigende Nachfrage in der Luftfracht.
/en/news/aktuelles-zur-weltweiten-transp.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Latest news on the global transport situation Latest news on the global transport situation Published - 8.4.2021 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard Air & Sea News April 2021 sea freight The situation, which had already been tense for months due to a lack of equipment, as we have already reported extensively, was brought to another unpleasant peak as a result of the blockage of the Suez Canal. We can already clearly see the effects: Rise in the price of shipping in April Further restriction of container availability due to lack of ship arrival Due to the congestion of 400 large ships in the Suez Canal, the onward journey (daily throughput of around 50 ships) takes place with some delay. As a result of the disruption created in the logistics chain, which has already been affected by the virus pandemic, the effects will be clearly noticeable for months to come. Ports are suddenly having to cope with increased volumes, and considerable delays in forwarding can also be expected at receiving ports. airfreight Air freight volumes are still booming, particularly when imported from China. Some importers have forced to switch to air freight (and also rail freight) due to the sea route blockage. This and the fact that there are hardly any passenger flights as the backbone of air freight mean that hope for a fundamental easing of price levels and cargo space is dwindling here as well. In general Extraordinary events and the continuing tense situation in the healthcare sector continue to make it difficult to plan international shipments by sea, rail and air. The rate level remains very high, unstable and barely predictable. Due to a lack of space and lack of equipment for all modes of transport, deadlines can only be implemented with an extended time window. We would love to send you better news and we hope to be able to do so again soon. In the meantime, we continue to ask for your understanding of the current situation, which we cannot influence. /en/news/anderungen-fur-strasse-schiene-.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Changes for road, rail, inland waterways and aviation Changes for road, rail, inland waterways and aviation Published - 3.1.2023 Reading time - 1 min Table of contents wildcard New dangerous goods regulations 2023 From 01.01.2023, new dangerous goods regulations will apply to modes of transport Road (ADR 2023) Rail (RID 2023) Inland vessel (ADN 2023) Aviation (IATA 64th edition) in force. The IMDG code for maritime transport (41-22) may be applied from 01.01.2023, but only comes into force from 01.01.2024. There is a 6-month transition period for road, rail and inland waterway modes of transport. Until 30.06.2023, the previously valid regulations (ADR 2021/RID 2021/ADN 2021) can continue to be applied. Emons Spedition GmbH will switch to the new law in mid-June 2023. /en/news/autotransporte-bei-emons-wenn-s.description: Safely transport supercars, collectibles & luxury cars — find out how Emons airfreight vehicles around the world every week.
/en/news/autotransporte-bei-emons-wenn-s.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Car transport at Emons: When supercars learn to fly Car transport at Emons: When supercars learn to fly Published - 24.10.2025 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard From Lamborghini's on airplanes and community love to PS: How our specialist transport for luxury vehicles became a successful social media series ‍ Anyone who only connects Emons with classic truck transport should be surprised when scrolling through our social media channels: luxury cars such as Lamborghinis, Ferraris, Bugattis and Koenigseggs, extensively secured on truck beds or on airplanes. This is no exception, but part of our daily business. ‍ We transport the world's most expensive cars every week Week after week, Emons transports some of the world's most exclusive vehicles — safely, discreetly and globally. In 2023, we loaded over 1,380 vehicles by air freight. That's an average of 27 vehicles per week, including genuine rarities, custom-made products or unique pieces in the seven-figure range. Customers who own such vehicles expect nothing less than perfection. And that is exactly what we deliver with closed special transport, individual customs processing and complete protection. Each vehicle has its own story and deserves our full focus. ‍ From a special mission to a community hit A few months ago, we came up with the idea: Why not show this to our followers too? This is how our social media series “Car Transport of the Week” was created. Every Friday, we present a vehicle that we have recently transported. Whether Bugatti, Koenigsegg, Rolls-Royce or Ferrari — our community is celebrating with us. And not just in a traditional logistics environment. The response is overwhelming: Our community loves the posts, shares, comments, speculates about the models. Some fans are literally waiting for the next transport. ‍ Why customers trust us with their most valuable vehicles The campaign shows that logistics must not only “work”, but can also fascinate. Behind each of these transports is a team that takes care of customs documents, secure loading, time slots at the airport and maximum discretion — with a lot of passion and professionalism. Because when a customer hands us their dream car, whether it's a mint-colored Ferrari F40 or a custom-made Mansory-Cullinan, that means trust. And we take that very seriously. ‍ Conclusion: What this sector means for Emons · Strong differentiation on the market: Not many logistics companies can claim to regularly transport Koenigseggs, Bugattis or McLarens. · Valuable social proof: The campaign shows our performance and appeals to emotional target groups at the same time. · Reach outside the logistics bubble: We reach people who might otherwise have nothing to do with transport, but are impressed by what we do. ‍ Would you like to have your vehicle transported safely, discreetly and professionally? Whether it's a showroom delivery, international collectibles or exclusive custom-made products: We ensure that your vehicle is in good hands. /en/news/batterien-entsorgen-neu-gedacht.heading: Emons | Battery: Rethinking Battery Disposal
/en/news/batterien-entsorgen-neu-gedacht.description: Emons Battery: Specialist in battery and waste transports. Fast pick-up, certified under §54 KrWG, active across Europe. Logistics that enable the circular economy.
/en/news/batterien-entsorgen-neu-gedacht.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Emons | Battery: Rethinking Battery Disposal Emons | Battery: Rethinking Battery Disposal Published - 26.8.2025 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard Rethinking Battery Disposal – How Logistics Powers the Circular Economy Whether in e-bikes, industrial machinery, or forklifts – lithium-ion batteries have become indispensable in modern industry. But once their performance fades, the complex part begins: where do they go? Disposing of batteries is not a simple process. They are classified as hazardous materials, subject to strict regulations, and pose considerable risks – from fire hazards to mandatory take-back obligations under battery legislation. For many companies, the logistics behind it are a challenge: a fragmented provider landscape, long waiting times, and burdensome documentation requirements. This is exactly where reliability becomes critical. While conventional providers often need up to four weeks to collect used batteries, Emons | Battery handles pickups within 5 to 7 working days – across Europe. That’s not just faster than the industry average – it’s more predictable and a real asset for companies looking to act responsibly. ‍ Clear focus: logistics only ‍ Emons | Battery remains clearly positioned: we are a logistics service provider. The actual recycling is handled by qualified partners – including the dedicated disposal network e.Punkt . But to keep circular processes moving, a strong logistics backbone is essential. That’s exactly what Emons | Battery delivers. This article explores why battery disposal is no longer just a compliance task, and how specialized transport solutions help companies meet their legal obligations and put circular economy into action. ‍ Battery Disposal – A Key Task That's Often Underestimated From cars and power tools to smartphones and industrial equipment – once batteries reach the end of their life cycle, they become both a risk and a resource. Aluminum, copper, lithium – just three of the valuable raw materials that can be recovered. At the same time, these batteries are hazardous goods that can become ticking time bombs if stored or transported improperly. Safe battery disposal means: compliant take-back, reliable transport, and a functioning network for further processing. ‍ Waste Transport With Integrity – What Emons Battery Does Differently The answer to this challenge comes from a familiar name in logistics – now in a new context: Emons | Battery. As an independent division of the Emons Group, Emons Battery specializes solely in transport services for (hazardous) waste and batteries. Thanks to certified partners and the e.Punkt disposal network, Emons | Battery has succeeded in closing the loop from take-back to recycling. The company acts as the perfect logistics interface – fast, compliant, and pan-European. ‍ What Emons | Battery Offers Hazardous goods-compliant battery transport across Europe – in just 5–7 working days Certified under §54 of the German Circular Economy Act (KrWG) Registered and authorized in many EU countries Integrated with the eANV (electronic waste record system) Battery container pooling for lithium-ion batteries Transparent communication – no call centers, real contact ‍ In practice, this means: Emons | Battery brings battery waste to the right processing partners – safely, reliably, and with clear documentation. /en/news/beware-neues-rebranding-gleiche.heading: BEWARE: New rebrand. Same DNA. More responsibility.
/en/news/beware-neues-rebranding-gleiche.description: BEWARE provides Europe-wide logistics for lithium-ion batteries, hazardous waste and recyclable materials. Secure transportation, container solutions, and recycling interfaces.
/en/news/beware-neues-rebranding-gleiche.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / BEWARE: New rebrand. Same DNA. More responsibility. BEWARE: New rebrand. Same DNA. More responsibility. Published - 9.3.2026 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard By rebranding Emons Battery to BEWARE, we are making visible what has always distinguished our work: special logistics at the highest level for sensitive substances such as batteries, dangerous goods, waste and recyclable materials — across Europe, in compliance with the law and quickly. Why a rebrand? The requirements for handling lithium-ion batteries, hazardous waste or exceptional goods are increasing. At the same time, there is a growing need for reliable partners who not only transport, but also understand, control and secure. With the rebrand, we are specifically positioning ourselves as an independent specialist service provider within Emons with a focus on: · Battery logistics over the entire life cycle · Special transport of sensitive, dangerous or particularly valuable goods · Waste and recycling logistics in close cooperation with certified partners · Europe-wide logistics solutions with comprehensive permits BEWARE stands for responsibility in a complex environment. For expertise where others become uncertain. For far-sightedness where others wave away. A look at our strengths Batteries We transport all types of batteries, from lithium batteries to mixtures. Whether as a product, return or waste. Always safe. Always compliant. Always predictable. Exceptionals From long goods to ammunition; from dangerous goods class 1 to dangerous goods class 9. Our special transports are as individual as the goods themselves. Includes approvals, planning, and documentation. Waste Waste is not a burden, but a process that must be precisely controlled. We assume responsibility for documentation, security and legally compliant transportation, including eANV and clear documentation. recycling We're thinking ahead. BEWARE is an interface between waste producer, transport and certified recycling with a network of certified partners. ‍ We do all of this not just individually, but in combination. We think in terms of solutions, not in individual logic. And we combine our strengths with Emons' network and experience under one strong roof. And that across national borders, because BEWARE has a strong network throughout Europe. Container logistics: Our silent superpower Without suitable containers, no safe transport. This applies in particular to batteries in a wide variety of shapes, states and hazard classes. What many overlook is that choosing the right container determines the safety and legal compliance of the entire logistics chain. BEWARE offers suitable container solutions for all battery sizes. /en/news/cbam-2026-neue-co2-pflichten-fu.description: From 2026, the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) will apply. Find out which imported goods are affected, which CO₂ certificates are required and how companies should prepare now.
/en/news/cbam-2026-neue-co2-pflichten-fu.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / CBAM 2026: New CO₂ requirements for EU imports — what companies are facing now CBAM 2026: New CO₂ requirements for EU imports — what companies are facing now Published - 2.2.2026 Reading time - 2 min Table of contents wildcard Introduction: What is CBAM? Since 01.01.2026, the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) has come into full force. The aim of the mechanism is to avoid so-called “carbon leakage” effects — i.e. the transfer of CO₂-intensive production abroad. This is intended to create a level playing field and strengthen European climate protection. ‍ Who does CBAM affect? Companies that import more than 50 tons of certain product groups into the EU each year are affected. The following applies to these: There must be approval as a CBAM applicant. CBAM applies in particular to imports of the following product groups: · Aluminum · Iron and steel (including downstream products such as screws, sheets, etc.) · Fertilizer · Hydrogen · Electricity · Cement ‍ What is changing in practice? From 2026, importers must prove and document the CO2 footprint of the affected goods. Depending on the emission value, CO₂ certificates may be required, which are based on European CO₂ prices. Specific obligations for companies: · CBAM registration and approval with the EU · Quarterly reporting on the CO₂ intensity of imported goods · Acquisition of CBAM certificates (mandatory from 2026) · Additional bureaucratic burden for imports from third countries ‍ What does CBAM mean for logistics? CBAM is an important topic for logistics service providers such as Emons. It not only affects the goods themselves, but also has an impact on customs clearance, processes, documentation and consulting expertise along the supply chain. Companies should coordinate with their suppliers at an early stage and, if necessary, seek support from specialized consultants such as Cologne Customs and Consulting. Our tip: Have your CBAM relevance checked at an early stage and ensure that all data sources for the CO₂ balance of your imported goods are available and reliable. The countdown is on! Published - Reading time - 6 min Table of contents wildcard Container sizes at a glance: Dimensions of 20ft, 40ft, and High Cube containers, as well as FCL or LCL. Find the right container solution for your sea freight. Container sizes play a central role when transporting goods internationally by sea. Whether it's machinery, commercial goods, raw materials, or packaged cargo: choosing the right container affects how efficiently a shipment can be planned, loaded, and transported. For companies, it is particularly important to know which container sizes are available, how 20ft and 40ft containers differ, and when a High Cube container makes sense. The decision between FCL and LCL is also closely linked to volume, type of goods, and shipping requirements. What does container size mean? Container sizes describe the standardized dimensions of containers. This primarily includes length, width, and height, as well as the usable interior space. In international trade, 20ft containers, 40ft containers, and 40ft High Cube containers are particularly common. Are you planning an international sea freight shipment and want to find the right container solution? Speak with the experts at Emons Air & Sea or submit your non-binding freight inquiry Which container sizes are available? Standardized containers are primarily used in international sea freight. 20ft containers, 40ft containers, and 40ft High Cube containers are especially common. They differ mainly in length, internal volume, and usable height. The specific dimensions can vary slightly depending on the container type, manufacturer, and shipping line. In addition to these standard sizes, there are other container types for special requirements. These include, for example, refrigerated containers for temperature-controlled goods, open-top containers for cargo loaded from above, or flat-rack containers for particularly heavy or oversized goods. 45ft High Cube containers may also be an option depending on the route and availability. For initial guidance, these questions are usually sufficient: How much volume does the shipment require, how heavy is the cargo, and are there any special requirements regarding height, temperature, or loading? Container sizes and dimensions at a glance Container dimensions are standardized but can vary slightly depending on the manufacturer, shipping line, and specific equipment. Therefore, these values should always be understood as a guide and verified for specific shipments. Hapag-Lloyd also notes in its own container data that specifications may vary by manufacturer. Containergröße Innenmaße Rauminhalt 20-Fuß-Container 5,90 x 2,35 x 2,40 m 33 m³ 40-Fuß-Container 12,03 x 2,35 x 2,40 m 68 m³ 40-Fuß-High-Cube-Container 12,03 x 2,35 x 2,70 m 76 m³ These values are for guidance only. Dimensions, payload, and availability may vary depending on the container type, equipment, manufacturer, and shipping line. How to choose the right container size The right container size depends on more than just the length of the container. The key is the interplay between cargo volume, weight, packaging, stackability, and the method of loading. For example, a shipment might require a lot of space but be relatively light. /en/news/eigenstromproduktion-bei-emons-.description: Photovoltaics at Emons: In 2025, we produce over 818,000 kWh of our own electricity and save more than 105 tons of CO₂. Find out how we use solar energy to supply our logistics sites and practice sustainability in everyday life.
/en/news/eigenstromproduktion-bei-emons-.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Self-generated electricity at Emons: How we supply our sites with solar power and save CO₂ Self-generated electricity at Emons: How we supply our sites with solar power and save CO₂ Published - 27.1.2026 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard The sun is shining and the meter is turning at Emons: At more and more Emons locations, we generate our own electricity. What sounds like a simple sustainability measure is in fact a well-thought-out component of our energy and climate strategy. With our own electricity production, we cover a significant portion of our electricity requirements, reduce emissions and strengthen our independence from external energy suppliers — an important aspect in times of rising energy costs and volatile markets. ‍ Production, consumption and feed-in: The figures for 2025 In 2025, we generated around 818 MWh of electricity from photovoltaic systems at our sites in Kenzingen, Cologne, Gengenbach, Thurnau and in future also in Uhrsleben. Compared to 2024, we thus produced around 50 MWh more of our own electricity and were able to save almost 3 tons of additional CO₂ at the same time. ‍ We used over 307 MWh of the generated energy directly for our own needs, in particular for: ‍ the operation of our shipping and logistics facilities charging our e-vehicles at company-owned charging stations our digital infrastructures at the locations ‍ Since in-house electricity production depends on the weather, electricity demand could not be completely covered by our own generation at all times. In low-sun months, external green electricity was also required. In the sunny months, on the other hand, we fed excess energy into the public grid: In 2025, over 510 MWh flowed back into the general power grid. ‍ ‍ CO₂ savings: over 100 tons per year ‍ By using self-generated solar power, we were able to save over 105 tons of CO₂. This saving relates exclusively to self-used electricity and represents a measurable contribution to climate protection. ‍ An example: The Thurnau site alone saved over 36.6 tons of CO₂ exclusively through the use of PV power in its own operation. ‍ ‍ Conclusion: Sustainable logistics requires smart energy Our investments in our own electricity production pay off in several ways: ecologically, economically and operationally. It is clear to us that the future of logistics will not only be digital, it will also be electric. And we are making the foundations for this visible today. ‍ Learn more about Emons' sustainability strategy: https://www.emons.de/portrait ‍ ‍ Teilen Link kopieren Reading progress Reading time More posts Publishes - 22.9.2026 Emons at #1: An award for the German SME sector Read the post Publishes - Container sizes at a glance: 20', 40', High Cube, and more. The ranking was published by the business magazine Markt und Mittelstand and is based on the DDW index from Die Deutsche Wirtschaft . A total of 39 criteria are included in the assessment, including company size, innovative strength, market position, and future viability. In recent years, we have further expanded our presence in regions including the Iberian Peninsula, Liechtenstein, and Vietnam. At the same time, we are strengthening our existing network where necessary through strategic partnerships and investments – most recently with Wolf Spedition. An external comparison of the top companies reveals an interesting aspect: Emons is not the largest company among the top three in terms of either the number of employees or logistics space. Differences, however, are evident in our international freight forwarding network and our own transport capacities. Freight forwarding and logistics with a broad service portfolio Our strength lies in our broad service portfolio, ranging from road and rail cargo to logistics and air & sea freight. This allows us to meet a wide variety of customer requirements and develop individual, one-stop solutions. At the same time, we are investing in the digitalization of our services. Digital booking options, transparent information, and connected services are designed to make logistics even simpler and more efficient for our customers in the future. Ranking #1 among the Top 50 freight forwarding and logistics companies is not only a special honor for us, but above all a motivation to continue on this path: expanding our international network, driving digitalization forward, and developing new solutions for our customers' needs. /en/news/emons-beteiligt-sich-an-der-wol.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Emons beteiligt sich an der Wolf Spedition Emons beteiligt sich an der Wolf Spedition Published - 23.4.2026 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard Rückwirkend zum 1.4.2026 beteiligt sich die Emons Spedition GmbH & Co. KG an der Wolf Spedition GmbH & Co. KG. Bereit seit den 60-er Jahren besteht eine enge partnerschaftliche Zusammenarbeit zwischen den beiden Speditionsunternehmen. Ziel ist es, die Stückgutaktivitäten in der Region zu stärken und auszubauen. Carolin Wolf, die auch weiterhin als Geschäftsführerin agiert und Ralf Wieland (CEO Emons) sind sich einig „Innovation aus Tradition“ sind Werte, die für beide Firmen gelten.“ Gemeinsam möchten Sie ein zuverlässiger Partner für die regionalen Speditionskunden bleiben, die Stückgutverkehre entwickeln und bei Innovationen und Digitalisierung ihre Kräfte bündeln. Die Beteiligung ist beschränkt auf die Wolf Spedition. Andere Unternehmensbereiche der Michael Wolf OHG, wie die Entsorgung und Logistik, fallen nicht unter die Beteiligung. Über Emons : Das eigenständige Familienunternehmen mit Hauptsitz in Köln wurde 1928 gegründet und beschäftigt heute rund 3.750 Mitarbeitende an weltweit 125 Standorten. 2025 erwirtschaftete Emons einen Umsatz von ca. 700 Mio. €. Das Unternehmen bietet Transporte auf Straße und Schiene, Luft und See sowie umfassende Logistik- und Zollservices und setzt auf zertifizierte Qualitäts-, Umwelt- und Informationsmanagementsysteme. Über die Wolf Spedition: Die Wolf Spedition ist ein familiengeführtes Unternehmen mit derzeit 150 Mitarbeiter*innen und ein Teil der Michael Wolf Unternehmensgruppe, welche sich auf die Schwerpunkte Spedition, Entsorgung und Logistik, sowie Luft- und Seefracht spezialisiert hat. Regional verwurzelt, aber weltweit in vielen Dienstleistungsbereichen tätig. ‍ Teilen Link kopieren Reading progress Reading time More posts Publishes - 22.9.2026 Emons at #1: An award for the German SME sector Read the post Publishes - Container sizes at a glance: 20', 40', High Cube, and more. /en/news/emons-expandiert-nach-spanien--.description: Emons is expanding to Spain: With the founding of EMONS LOGISTICS ESPAÑA and partner Grupo Tafatrans, we are strengthening our international network. Learn more about our values, goals and significance for the Iberian Peninsula as a location.
/en/news/emons-expandiert-nach-spanien--.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Emons expands to Spain - partnership with Tafatrans strengthens international network Emons expands to Spain - partnership with Tafatrans strengthens international network Published - 26.9.2025 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard A new milestone for our internationalization With the founding of EMONS LOGISTICS ESPAÑA, we are consistently continuing our internationalization strategy. From now on, we are also active in Spain with our own national subsidiary, thus completing our presence on the Iberian Peninsula. ‍ ‍ Together Stark with Grupo Tafatrans Our move to Spain is not done alone: Together with our partner Grupo Tafatrans, a traditional family company from Pamplona, we combine expertise and experience. Tafatrans brings almost 50 years of market expertise — with over 100 employees, its own fleet of more than 70 trucks and modern storage and handling areas. The range of services ranges from nationwide general cargo transport to partial and full loads to professional logistics services. ‍ ‍ Voices from corporate management “With our own branch in Spain, we are setting an important milestone in the development of our European network,” says Ralf Wieland, CEO of Emons. Arne Lingemann, Managing Director International, adds: “Together with Miguel Suárez and the strategic partnership with Tafatrans, we are creating the basis for offering our customers in Spain and the rest of Europe even more tailored and efficient logistics solutions. ” ‍ ‍ More than business: A partnership based on shared values For us, the cooperation with Tafatrans is more than just a strategic market entry. Both companies share fundamental values: reliability, customer focus, family orientation and long-term thinking. This shared attitude creates trust — both within teams and among our customers. This creates a partnership that not only pursues common economic goals, but also conveys a shared culture. We are convinced that in the logistics sector in particular, it is crucial that values such as sustainability, commitment and proximity not just remain words, but represent lived principles. ‍ ‍ Looking ahead With EMONS LOGISTICS ESPAÑA, we are now expanding our international network to 125 locations in 17 countries. Our goal remains clear: tailor-made logistics solutions from a single source — efficient, reliable and future-oriented. We are looking forward to the next steps and to shaping the Spanish market together with Tafatrans — and to connecting our customers even better across Europe. ‍ Teilen Link kopieren Reading progress Reading time More posts Publishes - 22.9.2026 Emons at #1: An award for the German SME sector Read the post Publishes - Container sizes at a glance: 20', 40', High Cube, and more. /en/news/emons-kenzingen-gewinnt-neuen-l.heading: Emons Kenzingen gains new logistics customer
/en/news/emons-kenzingen-gewinnt-neuen-l.description: Das Designunternehmen Aliseo lagert seine Logistik an Emons Kenzingen aus. Nachhaltige Logistiklösungen, CO₂-Reduktion und effiziente Distributionsprozesse.
/en/news/emons-kenzingen-gewinnt-neuen-l.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Emons Kenzingen gains new logistics customer Emons Kenzingen gains new logistics customer Published - 30.9.2022 Reading time - 2 min Table of contents wildcard Outsourcing logistics from Aliseo to Emons in Kenzingen The Black Forest design company Aliseo GmbH outsources its logistics from its current own logistics center in Gengenbach to the transport and logistics company Emons. In future, the goods will be stored at the Emons site in Kenzingen and distributed directly from there. Kenzingen is not only a logistics location, but also a freight forwarding facility with a transshipment warehouse. This eliminates the need for transport between warehouse and distribution warehouse. With shorter transport routes, CO 2 -Reduces emissions. Emons put the modern plant in Kenzingen into operation in March 2021. The energy is generated in-house in the sunny region using photovoltaics and heat pumps. In this project, Emons can contribute its expertise in sustainable logistics and look into a future of partnership together with Aliseo. “We are pleased that we were able to win Aliseo GmbH, which has a very good reputation on the market, as a strategic logistics customer for our logistics center in Kenzingen,” emphasizes Timor Spörl, managing director of Emons Logistik GmbH. Aliseo wants to continue to grow in the coming years. The larger capacity required for this will not be available at the current logistics location in Gengenbach in the long term. “We are very pleased to have now found a solution together with Emons that will enable us to set the course for this growth,” says Jan Hellfritz, managing partner of Aliseo GmbH, explaining the background of the outsourcing. Outsourcing is part of Aliseo's strategic reorganization. Production is to be brought back to Europe in the medium term to secure the supply chain. Aliseo also wants to be able to meet individual customer requirements in the hospitality and hotel industry even better. “This will be easier to achieve in Europe than is currently possible thanks to our production in Asia,” says Hellfritz. About Emons: Since 1928, the medium-sized and group-independent family business has stood for quality, trust and responsibility. With 3,420 employees at 100 locations in 16 countries, Emons offers transport (road, rail, air, sea), customs and logistics. Emons' logistics activities have been continuously advanced in recent years, so that logistics has become a strong pillar of the company. ‍ Teilen Link kopieren Reading progress Reading time More posts Publishes - 22.9.2026 Emons at #1: An award for the German SME sector Read the post Publishes - Container sizes at a glance: 20', 40', High Cube, and more. /en/news/emons-setzt-auf-elektromobilita.title: Emons News: Emons focuses on electric mobility: e-truck drives successfully through Stuttgart | Aktuelle Entwicklungen
/en/news/emons-setzt-auf-elektromobilita.heading: Emons focuses on electric mobility: e-truck drives successfully through Stuttgart
/en/news/emons-setzt-auf-elektromobilita.description: New e-truck at Emons: Since June 2024, an all-electric FUSO eCanter has been supplying customers in downtown Stuttgart — as part of the REALIST project. 100% CO₂ savings, over 12,500 km mileage and important findings for the city logistics of the future.
/en/news/emons-setzt-auf-elektromobilita.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Emons focuses on electric mobility: e-truck drives successfully through Stuttgart Emons focuses on electric mobility: e-truck drives successfully through Stuttgart Published - 14.10.2025 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard A new chapter in city logistics Since June 2024, an all-electric FUSO eCanter has been strengthening the fleet of the Emons branch in Ditzingen near Stuttgart. The vehicle supplies customers in Stuttgart city center on a daily basis and is part of the funded REALIST research project. Supported by the City of Stuttgart and its Climate Innovation Fund, the project aims to make inner-city transport more sustainable and to advance electrification in urban delivery transport. ‍ Successful interim results: More than 12,500 kilometers of electricity on the road After around a year in use, Emons is drawing a positive balance: The e-truck completed 164 tours with a total mileage of 12,571 kilometers. The project's goal — a minimum mileage of 11,000 kilometers — was thus significantly exceeded On average, the eCanter covered 77 kilometers per tour, transporting around 2.5 tons of goods for textile stores and small businesses in the urban area, among others. ‍ Full saving of CO₂ through green electricity In addition to its suitability for everyday use, the climate balance is particularly impressive. While a comparable diesel truck would have produced around 9 tons of CO₂ during the project period, the e-truck at Emons did not emit any CO₂ equivalents thanks to certified eco-electricity. This means that CO₂ savings in real operation are 100 percent. ‍ Stumbling blocks and solutions The path to zero-emission inner-city traffic was not entirely free of challenges. For example, the application for a subsidized charging station was rejected because the location was a few meters outside the city limits. Without further ado, Emons decided to finance the charging infrastructure out of his own pocket. There were also unexpected hurdles when it came to vehicle registration: Due to a software error, the eCanter could not initially be registered with an e-license plate. In addition, Emons had already gained experience with a failed e-truck project. Vehicles from a now-insolvent manufacturer were canceled because their range was not compatible with the requirements of everyday use. It is therefore all the more gratifying that the deployment within REALIST is now so successful thanks to a suitable selection of vehicles, a clear project structure and a strong partner. ‍ A strong team in the background A new driver was hired specifically to use the e-truck. Michael Bauer, who already wanted to give up the driving job, was convinced of the idea of electric mobility and has been driving the eCanter enthusiastically ever since. There were also internal changes: Rüdiger Bausch, who helped initiate the project, handed over branch management to his successor Marcel Schweiker in July 2024. ‍ Looking ahead: Further tests in Cologne Following the positive experience in Stuttgart, Emons is currently testing another e-truck at its Cologne branch. Here, too, the focus is on urban delivery and climate-friendly transport logistics. Current insights and updates on test operations are regularly available on our social media channels: 📲 Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn at [emons logistics]. ‍ Conclusion: Sustainable logistics starts today The use of Emons's first e-truck shows how climate-frien

/en/news/emons-ubernimmt-pall-ex-iberia.heading: Emons acquires Pall-Ex Iberia
/en/news/emons-ubernimmt-pall-ex-iberia.description: The Emons Group acquires Pall-Ex Iberia and continues to expand its European overland transport network. More capacity, better connection between Spain and Portugal to the Emons system.
/en/news/emons-ubernimmt-pall-ex-iberia.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Emons acquires Pall-Ex Iberia Emons acquires Pall-Ex Iberia Published - 5.3.2026 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard Strategic expansion with own network in Spain and Portugal Cologne, March 5, 2026 — The Emons Group is consistently continuing its growth path in Europe and acquires Pall-Ex Iberia. The acquisition marks an important strategic step for expanding Emons' European network structures. The takeover gives the company a comprehensive network with a central hub structure and strong regional partner depots in one of Europe's most important logistics markets. At the same time, the connection of the Iberian Peninsula to the European Emons system will be significantly strengthened. With the founding of Emons Logistics España in September 2025, the basis for an own operational presence in Spain was created. The acquisition of Pall-Ex Iberia is the next logical step in the company's internationalization strategy. “Integrating an established network in Spain and Portugal into our group opens up new opportunities for us in European land transport and creates tangible added value for our customers,” explains Ralf Wieland, CEO of the Emons Group . Arne Lingemann, Managing Director Road Freight International at Emons , underlines the strategic importance: “With Pall-Ex Iberia, we are gaining additional capacity and a fully developed network with a high level of regional market coverage. This is an important step for our international land transport and a lasting strengthening of our European system. ” Pall-Ex Iberia will continue to operate as an independent network within the Emons Group. The existing partner structures and business relationships remain unchanged. About Emons : The independent family company headquartered in Cologne was founded in 1928 and today employs around 3,750 people at 125 locations worldwide. In 2025, Emons generated sales of around 740 million euros. The company offers transport by road and rail, air and sea as well as comprehensive logistics and customs services and relies on certified quality, environmental and information management systems. About Pall-Ex Iberia : Launched in June 2011, Pall-Ex Iberia has consolidated its positioning in Spain and Portugal to deliver leading palletized freight distribution services through a network beyond 60 depots. The company has been recognized for its environmental efforts, achieving the Lean & Green 3-star certification for reducing its carbon footprint Press contact Emons Spedition GmbH & Co. /en/news/emons-ubernimmt-soziale-verantw.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Emons assumes social responsibility Emons assumes social responsibility Published - 15.11.2024 Reading time - 1 min Table of contents wildcard Helping together, moving together: An overview of our social commitment As a leading company in the logistics sector, we face not only economic but also social obligations. For this reason, we have once again decided this year to look beyond the limits of our core business and take on social responsibility. Because we are convinced that companies can and should make a positive contribution to society. An excerpt of our projects: • Carrying out and supporting several aid shipments to Ukraine • Donation and delivery of sports equipment, school supplies, jerseys and IT equipment to the Emons School in Kamituga (Eastern Congo) • Ball donation to the Regenbogenpaenz daycare center in Cologne Ensen • Donation of money to the Ludwig-Guttmann School Friends Association — Special Education and Counseling Center with a focus on physical and motor development — in Carlsbad • Donation in kind for the youth tournament “Eagle Cup” of the Cologne soccer club SV Adler Dellbrück 1922 e.V. • Taking over the transport of a customer's paper for delivery to daycare centers • Cooperation with Kölner Tafel • Taking over an animal sponsorship at Erfurt Zoo • Ball donation to DJK Südwest sports club in Cologne • School sponsorship runs for employees' children in Spornitz Our support is an expression of our commitment to the community. Because for us, social responsibility means living up to quality, trust and responsibility. /en/news/europalette-masse-gewicht-palet.description: Euro pallet overview: dimensions, weight, load capacity, and loading meters. Find out how many pallets fit into a truck and what is important for shipping.
/en/news/europalette-masse-gewicht-palet.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Euro pallet dimensions: weight & pallets in the truck Euro pallet dimensions: weight & pallets in the truck Published - 18.8.2026 Reading time - 6 min Table of contents wildcard The Euro pallet measures 1,200 × 800 x 144 mm and is a standardized reusable pallet for storage, handling, and transport. Its uniform size makes it easy to integrate into trucks, racking systems, and general cargo networks. Euro pallets are a logistical staple in warehousing, handling, and transport. They ensure that goods can be stored, moved, and loaded uniformly. For companies, it is particularly important to know how much space a Euro pallet requires, what weight must be factored in, and how many pallets fit into a truck. What makes the Euro pallet so versatile? Anyone shipping palletized goods needs a reliable basis for transport planning. The dimensions of a Euro pallet determine how much loading space is required, which vehicle is appropriate, and how accurately freight costs can be estimated. This makes Euro pallets a key planning metric, especially for general cargo, partial loads, and national road transport. Planning a pallet shipment? Submit your non-binding freight inquiry or contact our road transport experts. Euro pallet data: weight, load capacity, and shipment weight In practice, an empty Euro pallet usually weighs about 20 to 25 kg. For transport planning, a dead weight of around 25 kg is often used. The exact weight can vary slightly due to factors such as wood moisture, age, repairs, or the general condition of the pallet. It is important to distinguish between pallet weight and shipment weight. Pallet weight refers only to the empty pallet. Shipment weight, on the other hand, includes the entire shipping unit: goods, pallet, packaging, film, and strapping. Therefore, the gross weight of the shipment is always what counts for planning. For example, a pallet with 720 kg of goods, 25 kg of pallet weight, and 5 kg of packaging material results in a shipment weight of 750 kg. Weight affects not only freight costs but also vehicle selection. This is because a truck is limited not only by loading space but also by its permissible payload. Especially with heavy palletized goods, it should always be verified that the weight, weight distribution, and load securing are suitable for the planned transport. How many Euro pallets fit into a truck? The number of Euro pallets that fit into a truck depends on the loading length, interior width, payload, and loading method. As a general guide: a 7.5-ton truck often has space for about 15 Euro pallets, and a 12-ton truck for about 18. In practice, a standard semi-trailer usually holds 33 Euro pallets, or up to 34 if oriented optimally. Depending on the configuration, a truck-trailer combination can accommodate approximately 36 Euro pallets. In practice, weight, stackability, packaging, and load securing also determine how the shipment can actually be loaded. According to official EPAL data, the Euro pallet measures 1200 × 800 × 144 mm, weighs approximately 25 kg, and has a load capacity of 1,500 kg. For truck planning, Euro pallets are often calculated at 0.40 loading meters; a standard semi-trailer is typically specified as having 13.60 loading meters. /en/news/gefahrstoffspezialist-ldb-verst.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Hazardous substances specialist LDB strengthens Emons portfolio Hazardous substances specialist LDB strengthens Emons portfolio Published - 21.3.2025 Reading time - 4 min Table of contents wildcard Emons invests in LDB Group With retroactive effect from January 1, 2025, Emons is strategically investing in the LDB Group in Baden, which consists of the two operating units LDB Logistik GmbH and LDB Transport GmbH. The successful medium-sized company employs around 100 people. Major shareholder and managing director Torsten Fellmoser (57) continues to steer the fortunes of the LDB Group. The logistics service provider has locations in Bühl and Rastatt. The field of activity is divided into five business areas: warehouse/logistics and services, dangerous goods logistics, contract packaging, shop logistics and transport logistics. LDB Transport GmbH operates 30 of its own vehicles (mega trailers, trailer trains and jumbo vehicles), including an eActros 300. The LDB Group has made a name for itself, particularly in the area of hazardous materials storage. The capacities of LDB Logistik GmbH's hazardous materials warehouse at the headquarters in Bühl have just been increased to 8,100 parking spaces as a result of an expansion measure. At the same time, the entire hall was equipped with the latest sprinkler technology, fire protection technology and fire-fighting water retention technology. 14 different hazardous substances can now be stored in four storage sections. In addition, there is another hall with 1,600 parking spaces for harmless goods and a large work area for assembly work as well as 5,700 pick boxes for shop logistics. Two more warehouses for block storage complete the portfolio in Bühl. In Rastatt, LDB has 13,000 pallet parking spaces. Both family businesses focus on quality and close trusting customer relationships as well as sustainable action for the future. “LDB is the ideal addition to the Emons portfolio. Warehouse logistics in the hazardous materials sector is ideally suited to meeting the demands of our existing customers. LDB vehicles fit perfectly into our fleet expansion strategy. LDB's motto “Doesn't work — doesn't exist” is also exactly in line with Emons' philosophy,” explains Ralf Wieland, CEO of Emons. “Emons is strategically investing in the LDB Group. With our many years of expertise in hazardous materials storage, we complement Emons' range of services and at the same time benefit from the global network,” confirms LDB managing director Torsten Fellmoser. “It was also important to me personally that my professional life's work continues successfully. This works better in conjunction with Emons,” says Fellmoser. “In addition, it was just right from the start between Mr. Wieland and me. ” The new partners are looking forward to a harmonious and successful collaboration. The credo of both contract partners: We are stronger together! Emons and the LDB Group are looking forward to jointly marketing the additional capacities in the expanded hazardous materials warehouse, which will be officially opened in April, and to fully exploit the synergies of the partnership. ‍ About LDB LDB stands for Logistic Services Baden. The LDB Group combines LDB Logistik GmbH and LDB Transport GmbH. The new OSL Partnership wants to further expand the network's performance — with clear benefits for customers and partners. ‍ What does the OSL Partnership mean? With integration into the OSL general cargo network, companies benefit from: · Direct loading quotas via OSL hubs · Predictable delivery times for national and international general cargo shipments · High network availability through a comprehensive partner network Urmitz thus ideally complements the OSL partner network and further expands Emons' presence in the German general cargo segment. The Emons site in Erfurt has been active in the network as an OSL partner since 2015. With the addition of Urmitz, the system gains additional capacity, flexibility and regional strength. ‍ ‍ Focus on general cargo logistics General Cargo Transportation is a central component of modern logistics solutions, efficient, reliable and with fixed delivery times. The OSL Partnership makes processing even more transparent, faster and more predictable for customers. ‍ Outlook With the new OSL system partner status, Emons is once again underlining its position as a reliable logistics partner in the national and European general cargo network. /en/news/langere-laufzeiten.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Longer run times Longer run times Published - 20.7.2020 Reading time - 1 min Table of contents wildcard Current shipping planning As a result of vacation time, volumes are falling in particular (week 33-35) in southern countries such as Italy, Spain, Portugal, Greece, France and Turkey as well as the Balkan states. /en/news/leo-award-2025-fur-christiane-b.title: Emons News: LEO Award 2025 for Christiane Bauer: Why teamwork, courage and vision make the difference | Aktuelle Entwicklungen
/en/news/leo-award-2025-fur-christiane-b.heading: LEO Award 2025 for Christiane Bauer: Why teamwork, courage and vision make the difference
/en/news/leo-award-2025-fur-christiane-b.description: Christiane Bauer wins the 2025 LEO Award for the training project Why not Logistics. This is how Emons is tackling the shortage of skilled workers.
/en/news/leo-award-2025-fur-christiane-b.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / LEO Award 2025 for Christiane Bauer: Why teamwork, courage and vision make the difference LEO Award 2025 for Christiane Bauer: Why teamwork, courage and vision make the difference Published - 23.9.2025 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard At the 18th presentation of the prestigious DVZ LEO Award, Christiane Bauer, HR Manager at Emons, was honored in the “Manager” category — for her courage to break new ground, for her commitment to tackling the shortage of skilled workers and for a team effort that sets standards in the logistics sector. The jury thus honored their commitment to the “Why not Logistics” training project, which provides young people from West Africa with vocational training in Germany and brings urgently needed young talent to the industry. ‍ New ways to combat the shortage of skilled workers It quickly became clear to Christiane Bauer that things would not continue like this. The shortage of skilled workers in logistics was no longer just an issue, but a specific problem, particularly in the commercial sector. Traditional recruiting measures fizzled out and there were no applications. So she decided: We're rethinking it. This is how the “Why not Logistics” project was created, an international training program that specifically recruits young people from West Africa. A pilot who has now brought over 60 trainees to Germany. ‍ From pitch to award The idea for the project was further developed as part of the Emons | Digital incubation program. During the first pitch in autumn 2022, she was able to convince the jury at Emons Demo Day. Because Christiane Bauer not only had a vision, but also a clear plan: language as the key to success, close local support and intercultural competence as a basic attitude. On August 1, 2023, less than 12 months later, eight trainees from the Democratic Republic of Congo started at Emons. Today, there are already 28 more to follow this year: including young people from Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. Professional driver, warehouse specialist, warehouse logistics specialist and mechatronics technician are trained. Four women are also there. The program is closely linked with the Goethe-Institut, the BAMF and local authorities, and integration is actively supported. ‍ “This award belongs to all of us” For Christiane Bauer, the prize is one thing above all else: a team success. She expressly acknowledged the commitment of colleagues from the HR sector, the support of the Supervisory Board and the backing of the entire Emons workforce. She also emphasized the courage of young people who are starting their education in a new country: “You are a great motivation for us — and an important social signal. ” ‍ Emons breaks new ground The DVZ honored Bauer as a “determined, cosmopolitan and inspiring personality” who shows what modern personnel work in logistics can look like. And how important it is to actively address societal challenges instead of sitting them out. For Emons, the LEO Award 2025 is a special award and at the same time confirmation that our commitment can open up completely new paths, even in an industry steeped in tradition such as logistics. 🔗 Find out more about the “Why not Logistics” project and our training work in logistics at: www.whynotlogistics.de ‍ Photo: DVZ/Marco Grundt or DVZ/Hinrich Franck ‍ Teilen Link kopieren Reading progress Reading time More posts Publishes - 22.9.2026 Emons at #1: An award for the Ger

/en/news/lithium-ionen-batterien-boomen-.description: Emons ist Mitgründer des Entsorgungsnetzwerks e.punkt für Lithium-Ionen-Batterien. Sicherer Transport, Recycling und ein nachhaltiger Batteriekreislauf bundesweit.
/en/news/lithium-ionen-batterien-boomen-.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Lithium-ion batteries are booming. But where to put the waste batteries? Lithium-ion batteries are booming. But where to put the waste batteries? Published - 11.9.2024 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard Emons co-founder of the e.punkt waste management network Lithium-ion batteries are essential in numerous applications, from motor vehicles to mobile devices to e-bikes and energy storage devices. Almost anyone can and may transport new lithium-ion batteries. But what should you do when the end of life comes, the battery is defective or is recalled? In these cases, e.punkt comes into play and covers the entire battery disposal chain from packaging to transportation to recycling. e.punkt was founded by the LOGEX waste management network, logistician Emons, and recycling companies RE.LION.BAT. and STENA Recycling. All steps that a lithium-ion battery goes through from the point of origin to black mass are coordinated with the association of partners and their core competencies to ensure professional and environmentally friendly disposal. e.punkt organizes professional and environmentally friendly disposal. The tasks are clearly distributed: Everyone does what they do best. That is one of the guidelines among the founders. Emons is the first logistician to maintain a container pool for transporting critical batteries. Within 24 hours, the appropriate container can be made available at the disposal point via the Emons general cargo network. The packaged batteries are then safely transported — as a first step across Germany — to the Discharging & Dismantling Centers. There, the waste batteries are discharged and dismantled, significantly reducing the risk of fire posed by the batteries. Subsequent recycling produces the so-called black mass with valuable raw materials, which are returned to the cycle. A major advantage for customers is that batteries are moved over shorter distances in the partner network. This saves time, emissions and transport costs. Lukas Fast, authorized sales representative at Logex, summarizes: “The e.punkt network enables partners to concentrate on their core competencies. Germany-wide logistics and a smart container pool create efficiencies that were previously not available. ” “e.punkt offers customers the option of working with just one supplier for the nationwide disposal of lithium-ion batteries, which is an efficient alternative to a 1:1 relationship with several disposal companies. By limiting ourselves to the logistically sensible catchment area of our companies, e.punkt also increases our local capacity utilization,” says Arne Seeger, managing director of Stena Recycling. “The future of e-mobility starts with a sustainable battery cycle. The transportation of hazardous and non-hazardous battery waste requires extensive permits and reliable personnel with in-depth knowledge,” adds Enrico Hermanny, division manager of Emons | Battery. e.punkt with founders LOGEX, RE.LION.BAT, STENA Recycling and the Emons | Battery division has mastered this challenge. High quality standards, responsibility and safety in dealing with battery waste are the focus of all players. ‍ Teilen Link kopieren Reading progress Reading time More posts Publishes - 22.9.2026 Emons at #1: An award for the German SME sector Read the post Publishes - Container sizes at a glance: 20', 40', High Cube, and more. /en/news/ministerprasident-wust-zu-gast-.description: Emons Cologne welcomes Minister President Hendrik Wüst for an economic discussion. Topics: reducing bureaucracy, digitalization, and the future of locations.
/en/news/ministerprasident-wust-zu-gast-.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Minister President Wüst visits Emons in Cologne Minister President Wüst visits Emons in Cologne Published - 16.9.2025 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard A look at the future of Cologne as a business location On September 9, 2025, the Emons Cologne branch hosted a special exchange: Minister President Hendrik Wüst (CDU) visited our company as part of a business talk with regional entrepreneurs. The CDU's candidate for mayor in Cologne Markus Greitemann was also part of the event. Emons set the stage for a discussion on economic conditions and future prospects in Cologne in dialogue with entrepreneurs from the region. An insight into the world of logistics: tour of the Emons branch The evening began with a guided tour of our Cologne-based freight forwarding hall, accompanied by CFO Thorsten Heuser, HR manager Christiane Bauer, supervisory board member Herbert Putzmann and branch manager Stephan Schwarz. Mayor candidate Markus Greitemann also joined the tour. Particular interest was given to the current expansion of the warehouse and the daily scheduling processes. In the open-plan office, it was illustrated how digitization is already making its way into everyday life today — for example through the use of Smartlane, an AI-based support for route planning. It was emphasized that artificial intelligence does not replace people at Emons, but specifically supports specialists in making processes more efficient and saving resources. Here too, Emons remains true to its own line: sustainable through innovation, combined with social responsibility. In conversation with politicians: Reducing bureaucracy and future prospects This was followed by a moderated interview with Minister-President Wüst and candidate for mayor Greitemann in the foyer of the branch. The interviewees emphasized the need to reduce bureaucracy, digitize the administration and improve framework conditions to strengthen innovation, start-ups and Germany as a business location. Security in public spaces was also emphasized as a decisive factor for quality of life and economic strength. After an open Q&A session with the guests present, the evening ended in a pleasant atmosphere. Emons as a driving force in the region As a medium-sized family company with almost 100 years of history, Emons has always had close ties to the city of Cologne and the region. We are all the more pleased to have hosted this important exchange and, as a logistics company, to contribute to shaping a sustainable, competitive economic landscape. ‍ Teilen Link kopieren Reading progress Reading time More posts Publishes - 22.9.2026 Emons at #1: An award for the German SME sector Read the post Publishes - Container sizes at a glance: 20', 40', High Cube, and more. A total of 4,500 m² of space is now available for freight forwarding of general goods and for logistics activities. 2,000 m² is accounted for by a modular high-rack system with a height of 9.5 m. The warehouse is equipped with ten gates, an additional seven-meter wide covered gate for long goods and an access ramp. Approximately 350 m² of office space is available for administration. The logistics warehouse is partly occupied by existing business and still offers space for new customers. There is also the option to increase the storage space by an additional 3,700 m². Emons is now offering a reliable alternative with transport by truck. The duration of 35 — 40 days is just as attractive as the low prices. Cargo space is available at short notice. The time between booking and collection from companies across China is just 3 — 5 days. The goods are consolidated in the border town of Manzhouli. To round off the complete package, we can of course also offer our customers import customs clearance. Our Emons East department will be happy to receive your request and will quickly provide you with a competent and interesting offer. Your contact for Chinese imports by truck: Peter Seuss, e-mail peter.seuss@emons.de , telephone +49 9273 507-710. /en/news/news-kommissionierung-verfahren.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Definition, process, picking methods, and digital solutions Definition, process, picking methods, and digital solutions Published - 20.8.2026 Reading time - 6 min Table of contents wildcard Order picking explained: Learn about the different methods, how the warehouse process works, and what companies should look out for. In warehouse logistics, order picking determines whether goods are ready for the next process step completely, correctly, and on time. Whether for customer orders, production materials, or shipping: order picking involves retrieving items from inventory and assembling them according to an order. The more clearly the process is organized, the more reliably warehouse, packaging, and distribution operations work together. Order picking refers to the assembly of items from inventory based on a customer order, production order, or internal requirement. The goal is to provide the right goods in the right quantity and prepare them for packaging, shipping, or further processing. Would you like to connect your warehouse processes, order picking, and shipping more efficiently? Speak with our experts in logistics and road transport or submit your non-binding freight inquiry directly. Why order picking is important for warehousing and shipping Order picking connects inventory, orders, and shipping into a seamless process. Stored goods are transformed into a specific unit ready for packaging, production, further processing, or transport. This step is particularly important for companies because errors can have a direct impact on subsequent operations. If the wrong item is picked or a quantity is not assembled correctly, it leads to rework, delays, and additional costs. For order picking to function reliably, you need clear storage locations, up-to-date inventory data, understandable orders, and thorough checks. This allows warehouse, packaging, and shipping operations to integrate better, keeping the entire flow of goods more stable. How does order picking work in the warehouse? The order picking process begins with an order. This specifies which items are needed and in what quantities. Based on this, the appropriate storage locations are accessed and the goods are retrieved from inventory. After retrieval, the check follows. This involves verifying that the item number, quantity, and condition of the goods match the order. The items are then assembled and prepared for the next process step. This could be packaging, shipping, production, or internal transfer. The more clearly this process is organized, the lower the risk of errors. Especially when dealing with many items, multiple warehouse zones, or high order volumes, fixed processes, digital support, and a final check are essential. This turns inventory into a complete, ready-to-use unit for shipping, production, or further processing . What are the different order picking methods? There are various order picking methods used in warehouse logistics. The most suitable method depends primarily on the warehouse layout, the number of items, order volume, and requirements for speed and accuracy. Fundamentally, the goal is always to retrieve goods from inventory as efficiently as possible and prepare them for the next process step. One commonly used method is single-order picking. (IWS). The IWS is thus gaining an expert member from the international freight forwarding sector, especially in view of increasing globalization. The IWS acts as a link between industry and science. The focus is on influencing German and European politics in a non-partisan way with impulses for the benefit of the general public. The Senate represents SMEs — the success factor of the German economy. 99% of German companies belong to SMEs, which provide 60% of jobs and over 80% of training places. The IWS operates with the values of an “honorable businessman.” It stands for sustainability, social responsibility, ethics and morality. Education, the promotion of young talent and international orientation form the pillars of IWS. Wieland will bring inspiration from the medium-sized transport and logistics sector and thus optimally complement the network. “I consider it a great honor and a challenge to join the IWS as a Senator of Economics, which is one of the highest-grossing sectors in Germany but is only slightly noticed,” emphasizes Wieland. The awards ceremony as part of the summit took place on Friday evening, June 24, in Frankfurt am Main for all SMEs who were awarded the TOP 100 seal at the beginning of the year. The science journalist is accompanying the innovation competition, which is being held for the 29th time, as a mentor. In the scientific selection process, Emons was particularly convincing in the “Innovation-promoting top management” category. “We realized very early on that digitization would have an enormous impact on the freight forwarding and logistics industries and capitalized on the opportunities it offers us,” says CEO Ralf Wieland. As early as 2014, Emons acquired a majority stake in the start-up Cargo International. “This allows us to offer our private customers the opportunity to calculate their shipping costs online and book transport right away,” he explains. In addition, top management has initiated its own digital division, which focuses exclusively on opening up new digital business areas. /en/news/schwundkosten-auf-null-gesetzt.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Shrinkage costs set to zero from the beginning Shrinkage costs set to zero from the beginning Published - 5.11.2025 Reading time - 4 min Table of contents wildcard With the logistics shed, Emons Battery digitizes the management of expensive transport containers and thus prevents material loss ‍ Every lost container of dangerous goods costs money: Emons Battery uses special containers to transport lithium-ion batteries, which can cost tens of thousands of euros. To avoid losses, the Cologne-based company brought Logistikbude GmbH on board as a partner. With the digital platform for container management, Emons Battery always keeps track of its high-quality load carriers — and has banned material loss from its supply chain. At the same time, customers also benefit, because thanks to the logistics booth, it is possible to borrow on a daily basis, which saves costs. ‍ Since 1928, Emons has been offering a wide range of logistics and transport services. With its newest division — Emons Battery — the international logistics company is now entering a new field of logistics: battery logistics. Founded at the end of 2023, the division benefits from the efficient network and decades of experience of its parent company and offers ecological transport and disposal services for lithium-ion batteries and lead-acid batteries — internationally and over the entire life cycle of a battery. ‍ ‍ Expensive special containers: How Emons Battery provides access to safe transportation of dangerous goods ‍ Batteries are considered dangerous goods and must be transported in approved, fireproof containers, including in accordance with ADR guidelines (European Agreement on the Transport of Dangerous Goods by Road). The special thing about handling batteries: The person who places them on the market, i.e. sells or ships them, is responsible for their transportation and compliance with safety regulations. However, expensive special containers and proper battery disposal pose major challenges for many companies. Enrico Hermanny, head of the Emons Battery division, explains: “Depending on the intended use, the costs for special containers can amount to tens of thousands of euros. For many companies, these costs are difficult to bear. ” ‍ That's where Emons Battery comes in: The company offers its customers a complete package for battery transport. For example, if a defective battery has to be disposed of, Emons Battery provides the appropriate safety container, organizes transportation and ensures smooth delivery to the disposal point — whether it's a car battery or a battery for e-bikes. “In many cases, the container can be delivered to the customer within just 24 hours,” adds Hermanny. ‍ The focus is on maximum security and a reliable process. “For Emons, battery handling plays a central role in our sustainability strategy,” adds Hermanny. “With our new division, we are making the safe transportation and recycling of batteries more accessible and thus making a contribution to more sustainable processes. ” ‍ ‍ Container pooling with the logistics shed: digital transparency prevents high shrinkage costs ‍ As soon as the new division was founded, Emons relied on the logistics shop as an experienced partner for digital container management. /en/news/serap-guler-auf-sommertour-bei-.description: Staatsministerin Serap Güler besucht Emons in Köln und informiert sich über Why Not Logistics, internationale Ausbildung und Herausforderungen der Spedition.
/en/news/serap-guler-auf-sommertour-bei-.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Serap Güler auf Sommertour bei der Emons Spedition Serap Güler auf Sommertour bei der Emons Spedition Published - 7.8.2026 Reading time - 4 min Table of contents wildcard Staatministerin interessiert sich für das Ausbildungsprojekt „Why not Logistics“ und die Herausforderungen einer Spedition Köln, 4. August 2026 – Serap Güler und Reine Bredou trafen sich zufällig in Abidjan, Hauptstadt der Elfenbeinküste. Frau Güler lernte u. a. das Ausbildungsprojekt „Why not Logistics“ als Best Practice im Goethe-Institut kennen. Dort besuchte Reine den Deutschkurs als Vorbereitung auf ihre Ausbildung bei Emons in Deutschland. Heute war Serap Güler, Staatministerin des Auswärtigen Amts und Mitglied des Deutschen Bundestags (Wahlbezirk Köln-Porz), zu Gast. Im Rahmen ihres Zuständigkeitsbereichs für Afrika, Südamerika und des Goethe-Institutes tauschte sie sich mit Christiane Bauer, Leiterin HR Emons sowie Initiatorin von Why not Logistics (WNL), Thorsten Heuser (CFO Emons) und Norbert Maas (Betriebsleiter Emons Transporte) über die Herausforderungen in der Speditionsbranche aus. Im Vordergrund der Diskussion standen die Auszubildenden, die Emons aus Burkina Faso, der Elfenbeinküste und der Demokratischen Republik Kongo rekrutiert. „Ähnlich wie in der Gastronomie und im Bäckerhandwerk sind Speditionsberufe im Fahr- und Lagerbereich und auch Arbeitszeiten im Büro in den frühen Morgen- und Abendstunden nicht gerade sexy,“ berichtet Thorsten Heuser.  Es ist schwer Auszubildende zu finden.  Daher beschritt Emons vor fünf Jahren den Weg, sich Talente in Afrika zu suchen. Christiane Bauer führt aus „Wir haben es mit Berufskraftfahrer im Schnellverfahren ausprobiert. Daraus entstand keine Bindung ans Unternehmen. Über eine gute Vorbereitung, die schon im Heimatland beginnt und Entschleunigung während der mehrjährigen Ausbildung in Deutschland schaffen wir die Integration von motivierten und loyalen Arbeitskräften ins Unternehmen.“ Das Emons-Team von Why not Logistics besucht die Länder und führt dort die Bewerbungsgespräche mit den jungen Menschen selbst durch. Geeignete Bewerber für Emons und Kunden, die an dem Projekt WNL partizipieren, lernen beim Goethe-Institut Deutsch in ihrem Heimatland (Level B1) und erhalten eine Voreinführung in die Kultur. Emons übernimmt die Visa und andere Formalitäten und besorgt die Unterkunft auf dem privaten Wohnungsmarkt. Nach Ankunft in Deutschland durchlaufen die Auszubildenden ein einwöchiges Onboarding inklusive interkulturellem Austausch, an dem an drei Tagen auch die Ausbilder teilnehmen. Neben der normalen Ausbildung werden die Sprachkenntnisse mit geförderten Kursen auf ein Minimum von B2 gebracht. Mitarbeiter unterstützen bei Behördengängen, den alltäglichen Herausforderungen und der Integration über Sportvereine, Kirchen, etc.. Bei einem lebhaften Austausch mit anderen Auszubildenden aus dem Programm erzählt Christian, dass er alles an Deutschland mag, nur das Wetter nicht immer. Wenn es im Kongo heiß ist, denn geht wenigstens ein Wind. Nachdem er schon mit dem Sprinter Sendungen zugestellt hat, ist er stolz den Führerschein CE bestanden zu haben und jetzt im 3. Ausbildungsjahr mit dem großen 40-Tonner Lkw allein zu ersten Kunden zu fahren. Anfangs werden die Fahranfänger noch von Ausbildern begleitet, um Fahrpraxis zu bekommen. „Wir tragen eine große Verantwortung, junge Menschen mit großen Fahrzeugen in den Verkehr zu schicken und die nehmen wir sehr ernst“,
