/en/news/startschuss-fur-logistik-neubau.description: Emons investiert 16 Mio. € in ein neues Logistikzentrum in Thurnau mit 16.000 m² Fläche, nachhaltiger Energieversorgung und modernen Arbeitsplätzen. Fertigstellung 2021 geplant.
/en/news/startschuss-fur-logistik-neubau.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Starting signal for new logistics building in Thurnau Starting signal for new logistics building in Thurnau Published - 13.7.2020 Reading time - 4 min Table of contents wildcard Emons builds logistics plant in Thurnau With the symbolic groundbreaking ceremony on 10.07.2020, construction began for the new logistics center in Thurnau. Emons is investing €16 million in its new flagship Emons real estate. On the 3.5 hectare plot of land, we are building a warehouse complex with 16,000 m² of logistics space and 700 m² of office space. 16 gates and a ground-level access road will be available for delivery and distribution. The 14-meter high halls have 20,000 high-rack parking spaces and are equipped with a block warehouse plus a mezzanine. This second level for assembly work is 2,000 m² in size. The air-conditioned logistics facility is powered by ecological energy sources. With a photovoltaic system and an air heat pump, Emons is meeting its own sustainable and environmentally friendly requirements. This is supported by spacious green areas and the planting of trees. With a comfortable working environment and technical equipment that meets the latest requirements, Emons is setting new standards for its 50 employees. This will make Emons — in addition to the Himmelkron site with its 6,000 m² general cargo handling facility — an attractive employer with growth potential in the Thurnau region as well. The local proximity to a major customer and the interesting conditions in the municipality of Thurnau were decisive for the choice of location. The logistics warehouse should be completed in March 2021 and the move from the current location in Bad Berneck will take place. The new building provides space for existing customer and new business in the areas of warehousing, picking, packaging and other logistical value-added services. A 4K video system supports high security standards. The location will function as a customs warehouse with AEO-F status. With the groundbreaking ceremony in Thurnau, the third plant is currently in the construction phase, as planned. The new building in Kenzingen is now well advanced. In December 2020, the Freiburg freight forwarding branch will move into the plant with 3,000 m² of general cargo handling area and an additional 4,500 m² of logistics space. The groundbreaking ceremony for the 10,000 m² Gengenbach logistics center near Offenburg took place at the beginning of last week. Emons Logistik GmbH currently carries out high-quality, customer-specific logistics activities on 225,000 m² — with an increasing trend and in its own real estate, as can be clearly seen in the two latest construction projects. /en/news/stuckgut-versenden-definition-a.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Shipping general cargo: Definition, process & tips Shipping general cargo: Definition, process & tips Published - 20.8.2026 Reading time - 6 min Table of contents wildcard Not every shipment fills an entire truck. This is exactly where general cargo comes in: individual pallets, cartons, crates, or other packages can be bundled and transported with other shipments. For companies, shipping general cargo is particularly attractive when goods are sent regularly, but not in full truckloads. ‍ General cargo refers to individual, clearly defined packages or transport units that can be loaded, counted, and transported separately. This includes, for example, pallets, cartons, crates, barrels, or machine components. In general cargo shipping, these shipments are often bundled with other consignments and distributed via a transport network. Would you like to ship general cargo nationally or internationally? Submit your non-binding freight inquiry now or speak with our road transport experts. When does shipping general cargo make sense? General cargo shipping is primarily suitable for small to medium quantities of goods that cannot be sent via parcel service but do not require a full truck. This often involves individual pallets, spare parts, commercial goods, or deliveries to business customers, branches, and production sites. This shipping method is particularly useful when goods are sent regularly, predictably, and are well-packaged. By bundling with other shipments, available loading space is utilized more efficiently. This makes general cargo a practical solution for many B2B transports. For very heavy, bulky, non-stackable, or time-critical goods, a partial load or a customized transport solution may be more appropriate. The deciding factors here are primarily the type of goods, volume, transit time, and the requirements for pickup and delivery. General cargo, partial load, and full load compared Not every quantity of goods is transported the same way. Whether general cargo, partial load, or full load is the right choice depends primarily on how much loading space is needed, how heavy the goods are, and what the requirements are regarding transit time and delivery. General cargo is particularly suitable for small to medium shipments that can be bundled with other goods. A partial load makes sense when the quantity of goods already takes up a larger portion of the loading space but does not yet fill an entire truck. With a full load, the vehicle is used completely or almost completely for a single shipment. This distinction is important for companies because it influences planning, costs, and transit time. The more accurately packages, weight, volume, and requirements are known, the better the appropriate shipping method can be selected. For planning individual pallets, pallet dimensions and loading meters can also be relevant – for example, when determining how many Euro pallets fit into a truck. Not sure whether groupage, part load, or full load is the right fit for your shipment? Talk to our road transport experts or submit your non-binding freight inquiry . How does groupage shipping work? With groupage shipping, goods are not transported directly as a single full load, but are bundled and forwarded via a transport network. /en/news/tuv-rheinland-zertifiziert-emon.description: Emons strengthens its cyber defenses and receives ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification for information security in transport and logistics processes.
/en/news/tuv-rheinland-zertifiziert-emon.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / TÜV Rheinland certifies Emons according to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 TÜV Rheinland certifies Emons according to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Published - 3.9.2025 Reading time - 3 min Table of contents wildcard Emons protects its IT processes and strengthens cyber defense Cologne, September 02, 2025 — Being able to act for its customers and partners at any time is increasingly threatened by cyber criminals. Emons identified this risk early on and has consistently built up an effective information security management system (ISMS) since 2022. This allows effective protective measures to be combined to respond promptly and coherently to potential cyber security incidents. Building on this, Emons has had its central IT services to provide transport and logistics services certified in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022, the international standard for information security. The independent audit by TÜV Rheinland certifies that Emons Service GmbH has an effective management system and a high level of safety in transport and logistics processes. The certificate was presented by Ralph Freude (TÜV Rheinland), Ralf Wieland (CEO Emons) and René Koch (CISO Emons) at the company headquarters in Cologne on September 2, 2025. ‍ Advancing digitization and increasing networking of essential IT services offer areas of attack for cybercrime. As a medium-sized company in the transport and logistics sector, Emons is sending a visible sign of trust in a strong partner of secure supply chains, underlined with an internationally recognized certificate for information security. ‍ “Information security is business-critical for our transport and logistics services—from data transmission and shipment tracking to digital services. Certification in accordance with ISO 27001 is a strong sign of trust to our customers and partners along the supply chain. This underlines that Emons sees information security holistically as an integral part of its transport and logistics services and is systematically developing them,” explains Ralf Wieland, CEO of Emons. For Emons customers and partners, this means: ‍ · verifiably high level of protection of business-critical information in processes and IT systems for the provision of transport and logistics services · risk-based management and continuous improvement of safety measures through a structured management system · Transparency and reliability in audits and processes thanks to standardized procedures and regular reviews · higher resilience to cyber risks through continuous modification ‍ The Emons ISMS ensures the security of the company's customer, employee and partner data through clear responsibilities, documented technical and organizational controls, and a continuous improvement process. ‍ “Safe logistics requires more than powerful trucks. The successful certification was only possible because we worked consistently with our IT department on central security solutions. Through prioritized and coordinated measures across all teams, we were able to meet internal and external requirements — from policy work to audit preparation — and thus created opportunities for ourselves to make risks visible, react quickly in the future and be able to deliver reliably,” says Emons CISO René Koch. /en/news/vereinigtes-konigreich-grossbri.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / United Kingdom of Great Britain & Northern Ireland United Kingdom of Great Britain & Northern Ireland Published - 5.2.2021 Reading time - 6 min Table of contents wildcard Transport news to/from the United Kingdom of Great Britain & Northern Ireland Despite the Brexit deal, numerous customs formalities must therefore be fulfilled on both sides. Longer running times are to be expected until this settles in. We've put together the key points for you to ship your shipments to and from the UK. Unfortunately, we currently have to suspend shipments to private recipients, as GBPR customs is currently excluded in the UK. In order to avoid overloading the warehouse in England, it is necessary that the goods remain in the shippers' warehouse. Your checklist - export No private recipients, as customs clearance via GBPR procedures is excluded Export declaration (ABD, EX1, AE, MRN) starting at 0.01€ goods value 3-fold commercial invoice Who is responsible for import duties? The recipient's customs agent or Emons partner Does the recipient cover any costs? VAT 20% in the UK and any import duties/clearance costs Recipient's EORI number Contact person at the recipient with telephone number and e-mail address Delivery only after Avis. No appointments Since Brexit, pallets must comply with ISPM 15 Your checklist — import Before shipment: seller's commercial invoice. Request your invoice Exporter address and EORI number Importer's address and EORI number Importer contact details, email address, telephone number, and contact name Delivery address, if different from the importer's address Incoterms Invoice number Description of goods for each individual item Number of parts for each invoice item and summed up Net weight for each invoice item and summed Total gross weight Carton/pallet dimensions (unless an additional packing list is included Commodity code/HS code for each invoice item Billing currency If you have any questions about the changes caused by Brexit, please contact your local branch. Oder book Alternatively, a seminary with us. If you are interested, please click on the link . Certificate of preference Up to 6,000€, a “Declaration of origin” (eZu) from the exporter is sufficient (for individual or multiple shipments of identical goods for a maximum of 12 months) In excess of 6,000€, a declaration of the origin of the REX (Registered Exporter) including the REX number is required. You benefit from uniform administration and organization despite decentralized storage, which enables shorter distances to recipients. This reduces time and, in terms of sustainability, emissions in particular. Emons manages 44 logistics sites in Germany, Italy, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovakia. “For Emons, Warespace is an opportunity to cover white spots and thus work with customers whose volumes and location we cannot fully cover with our own storage capacities,” reports Timor Spörl. The modern and user-friendly Palletspace platform is also the solution for smaller customers who are looking for a quick and easy warehouse for a few pallets. /en/news/wirtschaftsdelegation-aus-turkm.heading: Business Delegation from Turkmenistan Visits Emons in Ditzingen
/en/news/wirtschaftsdelegation-aus-turkm.description: Emons hosts a business delegation from Turkmenistan in Ditzingen. The focus is on transport corridors, customs procedures, and logistics solutions between Europe and Central Asia.
/en/news/wirtschaftsdelegation-aus-turkm.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Business Delegation from Turkmenistan Visits Emons in Ditzingen Business Delegation from Turkmenistan Visits Emons in Ditzingen Published - Reading time - 4 min Table of contents wildcard Ditzingen, June 2026 – On June 26, 2026, Emons Spedition GmbH & Co. KG will host a high-ranking business delegation from Turkmenistan at its Ditzingen location. Participants include manufacturers of textiles, furniture, containers, chemicals, and foodstuffs, representatives of the oil and gas industry, service companies as well as representatives of the Ministry of Economy, Industry, and Construction of Turkmenistan. The visit will focus on economic relations between Europe and Central Asia, as well as the growing importance of efficient transport and logistics solutions for the region. The delegation will learn about current transport corridors, customs procedures, and the possibilities of multimodal transport chains between Europe and Central Asia. Emons has many years of experience in handling transports to demanding markets in Eastern Europe and Asia. Many years ago, the family-owned company specialized in niche markets such as Ukraine, the Caucasus, and Central and East Asia, building extensive networks and market knowledge there. A current example of this expertise is the successful execution of a project order to Turkmenistan. Emons transported essential components for the TAPI natural gas pipeline from Europe to Turkmenistan. This international energy project connects Turkmenistan's natural gas reserves via Afghanistan and Pakistan to the Indian market and is one of the most significant infrastructure projects in the region. The execution of these transports placed high demands on planning, customs clearance, and coordination along several international transport corridors. “The economic development of Central Asia opens up new opportunities for industry, trade, and logistics. The delegation's visit offers an excellent opportunity to deepen existing relationships and showcase the efficiency of modern logistics solutions for these important growth markets,” explains Emons' management. The visit of the Turkmen business delegation underscores the increasing importance of Central Asia as an economic and energy region, as well as the role of efficient logistics providers as a bridge between the markets of Europe and Asia. About Emons: Since 1928, Emons, an independent, medium-sized family business, has stood for reliable and flexible transport and logistics services. Today, the company employs approximately 3,900 people across 122 locations in 15 countries, generating an annual turnover of 667 million euros. Its service portfolio includes national and international road, rail, air, and sea freight transport, customs services, contract logistics, and digital logistics solutions. Emons boasts a powerful infrastructure for implementing complex transport and logistics projects worldwide. /en/news/zustellungen-mit-mitnahmestaple.searchText: Back to the overview Back to the overview Home / News / Deliveries with truck-mounted forklift Deliveries with truck-mounted forklift Published - 11.3.2022 Reading time - 2 min Table of contents wildcard Emons expands its product portfolio The need to deliver bulky and cumbersome goods on land that is sometimes difficult to access has increased during the pandemic with the increase in B2C shipments. Emons has added a technical solution to this challenge to its portfolio. With special vehicles, Emons delivers shipments even when access is restricted and unloading equipment is missing on site. The new service is interesting for demanding deliveries • on construction sites • beyond the curb on plots of land, in driveways, carports, etc. • in case of access restrictions for trucks • in dead ends without turning points • of large, long and bulky goods • of shipments that cannot be unloaded with a lift The trucks have a lifting capacity of 2,500 kg. With all-wheel drive, 4-way function and switchable differential lock, they are suitable for off-road use. Adjustable forks ensure optimal handling of long goods. The range of the 6 km/h truck-mounted forklift is 100 m. The forklift requires a width of at least 3 m and a height of 2.80 m for manoeuvring. The vehicles with this special equipment are strategically distributed at six locations (Cologne, Bayreuth, Villingen-Schwenningen, Saterland, Magdeburg and Chemnitz) in Germany. They deliver to customers within a larger area. The branch was established following the acquisition of the long-standing Mittelrhein Spedition Gith and has since become an integral part of the global Emons network, featuring a dispatch team with local expertise in Middle Rhine transport routes. Koblenz is located at the German Corner, where the Moselle and Rhine rivers meet, placing it on the vital Rhine axis between Cologne and Frankfurt. From Urmitz, Emons quickly reaches the region's economic hubs and the national and European distribution network via the A61 and A48 motorways, as well as the B9 federal highway running along the Rhine. ‍ Submit a freight inquiry now Submit a freight inquiry now Private customers Private customers Services at this location What our Urmitz branch offers the greater Koblenz area: ‍ General cargo system transport – Regular groupage services for the Middle Rhine, integrated into our supra-regional distribution network. Part and full loads – Direct transport along the Cologne–Frankfurt Rhine axis and to other European countries. Regional distribution – Last-mile delivery in the Rhine-Moselle region using our own fleet based in Urmitz. Warehousing & Handling – Handling and storage at our Urmitz site, serving as the link between procurement and distribution. Scheduled & Express Shipments – Time-definite transport via the A61 and A48, wherever the route allows. Rhine Corridor Connection – Short distances to the Cologne/Bonn metropolitan area in the north and Mainz/Frankfurt in the south. /en/munz-ldb.description: Sichere Gefahrstofflogistik & Fulfillment in Süddeutschland. Zertifiziert, skalierbar und effizient – jetzt Beratung anfragen.
/en/munz-ldb.searchText: Home / Munz-LDB Gefahrstofflogistik & Fulfillment in Süddeutschland: Ihre Supply Chain sicher skaliert. Durch unsere strategische Partnerschaft zwischen Emons und der LDB Gruppe bündeln wir globale Transportstärke mit regionaler Speziallogistik. Profitieren Sie von zertifizierten Gefahrstofflagern, maßgeschneidertem Contract-Packaging und einem spezialisierten Fuhrpark auf nationalen Strecken. Wir reduzieren Ihre Schnittstellen und machen Ihre Supply Chain effizienter und effiktiver. Ihre Supply-Chain mit Emons und LDB Zertifizierte Sicherheit für sensible Güter Wir übernehmen die rechtssichere Lagerung und das Handling Ihrer Gefahrstoffe in hochmodernen, zertifizierten Anlagen im Raum Baden. Value-Added-Services, die Fixkosten senken Mehr als nur Transport: Mit stückgenauem Pick & Pack, Qualitätskontrollen und Konfektionierung/Montagen direkt am Hub sparen Sie wertvolle Zeit, interne Ressourcen und letztendlich Kosten. 30.000 Palettenstellplätze in Süddeutschland Maximale Skalierbarkeit für Ihre Bestände. Unsere Block- und Hochregallager puffern Ihre saisonalen Spitzen und garantieren höchste Warenverfügbarkeit. Spezial-Fuhrpark für maximale Flexibilität Ob Jumbofahrzeug, Hebebühne oder Mitnahmestapler – wir stellen Ihre Fracht exakt dort zu, wo sie gebraucht wird, unabhängig von der Laderampen-Infrastruktur des Empfängers, oder auch auf Baustellen. Gefahrstofflogistik ohne Kompromisse: Sicherheit, Compliance und Effizienz Der Umgang mit Gefahrstoffen und sensiblen chemischen Produkten duldet keine Fehler. In der Gefahrstofflogistik geht es längst nicht mehr nur um den Transport von A nach B – entscheidend sind strenge gesetzliche Vorgaben, eine lückenlose Dokumentation sowie der Schutz von Mensch und Umwelt. Bereits ein kleiner Compliance-Verstoß oder Fehler bei der Ladungssicherung kann hohe Strafen nach sich ziehen und im schlimmsten Fall die gesamte Supply Chain beeinträchtigen. Ebenso haftet jeder Prozessbeteiligte persönlich. ‍ Lückenlose rechtliche Compliance: Gesetze und Sicherheitsdatenblätter ändern sich laufend. Wer Gefahrstoffe lagert oder transportiert, muss komplexe Regelwerke wie TRGS510 und ADR bis ins Detail kennen und korrekt anwenden. ‍ Zertifizierte Infrastruktur: Standard-Logistikzentren reichen hier nicht aus. Notwendig sind spezialisierte Brandschutzkonzepte, getrennte Lagerbereiche unter Beachtung von Zusammenlagerungsverboten sowie Rückhaltesysteme für flüssige Stoffe. Sowie automatische Löschanlagen und Brandmeldesysteme. ‍ Geschultes Fachpersonal: Von der korrekten Klassifizierung und Etikettierung bis zur Erstellung der Beförderungspapiere – fundiertes Fachwissen ist der Schlüssel für eine sichere Gefahrgutabwicklung. Ob Gefahrgut, Batterien, Sperrgut oder Sondertransporte – wir bieten Ihnen sichere, regelkonforme und individuell abgestimmte Logistiklösungen.Prof
